claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl with 15–45 μm feedstock is suitable for HVAF-i7 deposition.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces acceptable coating quality.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces insufficient coating thickness.
Changing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to 300–350 mm will increase particle velocity.
Increased particle velocity will increase in-flight particle kinetic energy.
Greater particle kinetic energy will increase impact and deformation upon substrate contact.
Greater particle impact and deformation will improve coating cohesion and substrate bonding.
Higher impact energy will promote better in-flight melting.
Increasing particle velocity will improve deposition efficiency through stronger particle-to-particle and particle-to-substrate bonding.
A 300–350 mm spray distance will increase coating thickness relative to the baseline HVAF-i7 process.
The intervention will produce a more adherent coating than the baseline process.
The intervention will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The thicker coating will retain acceptable quality and oxidation resistance during elevated-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention will remain effective when coating substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The effective operating window is limited to HVAF-i7 nozzle distances between 300 and 350 mm.
The intervention's effectiveness may depend on equipment calibration and may not transfer to other HVAF systems or substantially different feedstock sizes.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator attributes the benefit to kinetic energy causing deformation at impact, whereas the mechanism says higher impact energy promotes in-flight melting. Impact occurs after flight, so impact energy cannot itself cause an earlier in-flight event; no separate thermal pathway is provided.
